quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
rationale: Commerce One gives a full IP infringement indemnity covering us and our Customers, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics and procure-modify-replace-or-refund remedies, and only the usual exclusions (use outside Documentation, third-party modification). The indemnity sits entirely outside the Section 9 cap, which is better than the fallback super-cap, and there is no reciprocal Customer indemnity. Preferred extras (breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) are absent but that is short of the preferred wording only, not a fallback failure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot let our own interface code and configurations transfer to Commerce One simply because Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis; ownership of what we build stays with us, with Commerce One keeping its pre-existing IP.

ops.newText: shall be owned by Corio. Commerce One shall not acquire any ownership rights, including
ops.oldText: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including

ops.newText: intellectual property rights, in the Developments. To the extent
ops.oldText: intellectual property rights in the Developments. To the extent

proposal.summary: Delete the clause that vests Corio-created Developments in Commerce One where it supports them

quote: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
rationale: Section 13.5 vests our own interface code and hosting Developments in Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor with no licence back, which is walk-away territory under this rule. Redline deletes the "unless supported" reversal so Developments created by us stay ours while Commerce One keeps its pre-existing materials and the Software itself (Section 2.8, which is acceptable). We also note that ownership of enhancements to the Software developed by us is left to future negotiation.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept a mutual 12-month fee cap, but the cap must not be sliced down to the fees for a single "transaction", and confidentiality breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud must sit outside the cap alongside the Section 8 indemnity.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 10 OF THIS AGREEMENT, AND A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD.
ops.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.

proposal.summary: Make the cap a true 12-month fee cap and add standard uncapped carve-outs

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION
rationale: The cap is mutual and nominally 12-month based, but it is narrowed to amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to", i.e. materially less than 12 months' fees, and the only carve-out is Section 8 (indemnification). Confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud sit inside the cap, so the clause fails the fallback which requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Redline restores a full 12-month fee cap and adds an Excluded Claims sentence; the mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is acceptable as drafted.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required
rationale: The clause is mutual and carries an M&A/asset-sale carve-out permitting assignment without consent, meeting the fallback, and there is no Commerce One termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. Two sub-optimal points noted rather than flagged: the consent standard is not expressly "not to be unreasonably withheld", and the direct-competitor exception could require consent for an acquisition by a Commerce One competitor.

quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
rationale: No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements obligation binds us: all licences are expressly non-exclusive and nothing bars us from procuring or hosting competing e-procurement software. The only Vendor-side restrictions (Section 2.4 referral obligations on Commerce One not to approach our Customers) run in our favour and are not flagged.

quote: License Fees: Due upon Software Acceptance.
rationale: Neither the Fees section nor Exhibit B contains liquidated damages, penalties, shortfall charges, late-payment interest or minimum fees on termination payable by us; searches for "liquidated" and penalty-style amounts return nothing. Nothing to redline.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
rationale: The hosting licence is perpetual and irrevocable, permits unlimited sublicensing to our Customers, survives termination (Section 11.3), is transferable to a successor via Section 14.1, and Section 14.8 confirms we may subcontract delivery of the Corio Services; the internal-use licence is perpetual and fully paid up. Affiliates are not expressly named and the Territory is limited to North America (with an expansion mechanism in Section 2.10) — noted, but the grant meets the fallback on its material terms.

quote: "CORIO MARKET SEGMENT" means those customers with annual sales revenues of less than $1,000,000,000.
rationale: There is no covenant restricting the businesses we may operate, the products we may build or the competing offerings we may host or sell; the Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation is expressly non-binding. The Corio Market Segment and Territory definitions limit the scope of the licence granted to us rather than restrict our business, and Section 2.10 gives us an expansion path with consent not to be unreasonably withheld — noted, but not a field-of-use restrictive covenant.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A five-year committed term with no exit other than for breach is outside our position; we need a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees. We can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: 11.1.1 Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.summary: Add a Corio termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund

quote: The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
rationale: There is no termination-for-convenience right for either party during the five-year initial term; Section 11.2 allows termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. Absence of a Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation, so we add a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Helpfully, Commerce One likewise has no convenience exit, so no deletion is needed on that side.

quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection. If any such inspection discloses a shortfall or an overpayment, the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment.
rationale: The audit right is limited to once per calendar year, conducted by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to us, at Commerce One's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and gives no access to our systems — this meets our preferred position. Only the notice period is expressed as "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30/15 days, which we note rather than flag.

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods.
rationale: California law with AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco County, and judgment enforceable in the California courts, sits within our accepted fallback (California law and forum) and is nowhere near walk-away territory, which is reserved for an unlisted home jurisdiction or a foreign arbitration seat. We note only that we prefer courts to mandatory arbitration; that is a preferred-position point, not a deviation.

quote: MARKETSITE.NET SERVICE FEES: MarketSite.net Service Access: Year 1 [*] Year 2-5, and beyond: [*]
rationale: Exhibit B and the Section 4 fee provisions contain fixed pricing and revenue-sharing percentages with no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation running against us, and no obligation to extend Commerce One terms given to third parties. Nothing to redline.

quote: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
rationale: There is no take-or-pay, volume commitment or shortfall payment binding us: fees are fixed licence, maintenance and MarketSite access fees plus a revenue share on actual Customer revenue, and implementation work is time-and-materials capped. The "minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer" only sets the boundary of the revenue-share exemption for the pre-paid 3,000 user licences; it does not oblige us to purchase volume, and Software Users are unlimited.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: Commerce One represents and warrants that all Commerce One employees, agents, contractors or consultants that will be provided to work together with Corio have or will have signed agreements with customary terms containing confidentiality provisions and assignment of inventions
rationale: A full-text search for solicitation, no-hire and inducement language returns nothing; the personnel provisions in Section 13 and Exhibit D impose no hiring restriction on us. The absence of any non-solicit favours us, so no redline.

quote: this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement
rationale: Renewal terms are 12 months with a 30-day non-renewal notice window, which meets our preferred position on both length and window. Exhibit B fixes maintenance and MarketSite access pricing for Years 2-5 "and beyond", so there is no uncapped uplift mechanic; the absence of a Vendor renewal reminder and an express CPI/3% cap is noted only.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.3 addresses Confidential Information but not our exit: we need transition assistance and the return of Corio and Customer data held in the MarketSite.net Service in a machine-readable format, with certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Data Return. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all Corio and Customer data in its possession in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing.

proposal.summary: Add transition assistance and data return on expiry or termination

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Section 11.3 gives useful continuity (surviving licence, surviving support and Section 12 escrow) but contains no transition assistance and no obligation on Commerce One to return or export our and our Customers' data held in the MarketSite.net Service, nor any deletion certification. For a hosted arrangement that absence is a deviation, so we insert a fallback-level transition and data-return paragraph.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 60-day warranty running from the Effective Date and expiring on a fixed calendar date can lapse before the Software is even accepted; our fallback is 90 days from acceptance with the existing correct/replace/refund remedies unchanged.

ops.newText: for a period of ninety (90) days from the date of Corio's acceptance of the Software (the "Warranty Period")
ops.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")

proposal.summary: Extend the warranty period to 90 days from acceptance and remove the fixed calendar cut-off

quote: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
rationale: The conformance warranty runs only 60 days from the Effective Date and expires on a hard calendar date, so it falls short of the 90-day software fallback and can lapse at or before acceptance (acceptance testing itself runs to 31 December 1999). The remedies (correct, replace, terminate and refund prepaid fees), the no-malicious-code and IP warranties are otherwise adequate, so the redline only extends the period to 90 days from acceptance.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant; as Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service and its personnel work alongside ours, we ask for standard E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request (numbering to follow on renumbering of Section 14).

ops.text: 14.11 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Commerce One shall provide certificates of insurance to Corio on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a short insurance covenant in Miscellaneous

quote: 14.10 Complete Understanding. This Agreement including all Exhibits, and the Non Disclosure Agreement and the Statement of Work referenced in this Agreement and incorporated by reference herein, constitutes the final, complete and exclusive agreement between the parties
rationale: There is no insurance clause anywhere in the Agreement (the only hit for "insurance" is in the Application Management Revenue definition), and Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service through which our Customers transact and supplies on-site personnel. We insert a short covenant at the fallback level (CGL, E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request).
